A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffProxy, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable and comparable. Neither contains an appendix, although both refer to supplementary Algorithm 1. That unavailable algorithm cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, qualitative reconstructions, and ablations of hand refinement, view count, stochastic sampling, network modules and camera calibration.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results and ablations, including newly reported comparisons with DensePose and its fine-tuned variants.

M1.justification: Mesh fitting changes substantially: v1 Section 4.3 uses VPoser body latents, MANO hand PCA and L-BFGS to minimize reprojection loss. v2 Section 3.3 uses axis-angle poses, Adam and an added DPoser-X denoising prior weighted by 0.1. The diffusion proxy generator and basic aggregation rules remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The training-source families, five real-world benchmarks, partial-observation setting and estimated-camera evaluation remain. However, v1 explicitly evaluates single-view reconstruction in Table 3 and Figure 6; v2's corresponding Figure 8 evaluates only two, four and eight views. This modestly narrows the tested observation conditions.

E2.justification: The six main Table 1 baselines remain unchanged. v2 adds DensePose and variants fine-tuned on the synthetic training data for 30 and 60 epochs in Figure 9; Table 3 quantitatively compares original DensePose and the 60-epoch variant on MoYo. These were not evaluated comparators in v1.

E3.justification: v1 samples 100 scenes per dataset and averages single-view baseline errors across cameras. v2 specifies dataset-dependent splits, fixed camera selections and frame strides, and reports each single-view baseline's lowest-MPVPE camera per dataset. The reported synthetic training set decreases from 108,491 to 105,487 samples, default stochastic sampling changes from K=5 to K=3, and the new DensePose comparisons introduce 30- and 60-epoch fine-tuning protocols.

E4.justification: v2 expands hand-refinement and test-time-scaling ablations across all six Table 1 settings, adds a discriminative-versus-diffusion proxy study, and documents a fitting failure in Figure 10. Conversely, v1's hand-only quantitative evaluation, single-view reconstruction result and isolated uncertainty-weighting ablation disappear. Network-module and estimated-camera studies remain, combined in v2 Table 2.

E5.justification: The default number of stochastic predictions used to estimate per-pixel uncertainty decreases from five to three. The variance and majority-agreement estimators remain unchanged. This concerns inference-time uncertainty estimation; neither version adds benchmark confidence intervals, significance tests or variability across independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation results are extensively revised. For example, Table 1 reports DiffProxy's MoYo MPVPE as 56.2 mm in v1 and 38.8 mm in v2, while 4D-DRESS partial MPVPE changes from 34.2 to 43.1 mm. These are results under changed method and evaluation settings, not controlled gains or losses. v2 also adds component-ablation results across datasets and quantitative DensePose comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 7 changes the mathematical fitting objective from reprojection minimization to L_reproj + 0.1 L_prior, introducing explicit pose regularization. The diffusion and pixel-uncertainty equations otherwise remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is introduced; omission of v1's standard barycentric-interpolation formula is primarily explanatory compression.

C1.justification: The principal claims about synthetic-only training, dense proxies, hand refinement, test-time scaling and performance across five benchmarks remain. v2 adds an explicit claim that intermediate-representation quality is the central bottleneck, promotes the synthetic dataset to a standalone contribution, and emphasizes precision-oriented fitting in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations of dense constraints versus sparse keypoints and direct regression, including an explanation that hand refinement improves arm orientation. It also adds a specific limitation: correct proxies can still yield depth-inverted joints through fitting local optima, illustrated in Figure 10, with complementary 3D constraints proposed as a remedy. Runtime discussion now distinguishes the inexpensive base configuration from hand refinement and sampling.

D1.justification: v2 documents training-motion exclusions, evaluation splits/cameras/frame strides, UV-channel encoding, crop-adjusted camera intrinsics, the pose-prior weight, convergence thresholds and inference hardware with configuration-specific timings. Some detail is lost: v1's explicit fitting learning rate and 50-step denoising count are not retained, and numerical Adam fitting rates are unspecified. The project-page access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work as reviving dense-correspondence fitting against end-to-end regression and sparse-keypoint fitting. It drops v1's explicit first-use claim for multi-view diffusion in dense HMR correspondence. References newly include DPoser-X, Unite the People, LCR-Net++ and Consistency Models, while several registration/reconstruction references, including RVH Mesh Registration, Function4D and DeepHuman, disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental interpretation and conclusion are extensively rewritten around precise fitting and intermediate representations. The separate Overview section is absorbed into Method, related work separates end-to-end and fitting-based approaches, and Jun Li is added to the author list.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one and substantially revises its displays: the teaser is replaced, the pipeline is redrawn, Table 1 gains ablation rows and colored rankings, and camera/module tables are merged. Sampling-count and view-count tables become plots. Dedicated synthetic-data, DensePose-comparison and failure-case figures are added.

improvement.justification: The clearer evaluation protocols, direct DensePose controls and explicit fitting-failure analysis make v2's central argument better supported and easier to assess. The gain is limited by removal of hand-only quantitative evidence and the isolated uncertainty-weighting control, plus incomplete details for the new fitting optimizer. Changed methods and protocols also prevent treating revised benchmark scores as evidence of improved accuracy under identical conditions.
